tasks.short: Locate unusual information for a specific request.

steps.what: Clarify the unusual information request, relevant names and dates, intended use and acceptable evidence
Search the library catalogue, licensed indexes and archival finding aids for actual records matching the specific question
Open the candidate sources, resolve identities and unusual terminology, verify the requested fact and pursue missing evidence manually
Prepare and check the response with verified findings, exact source references, access limits and the intended requester
outputs: approved research response v1 and recipient

steps.what: Send the exact approved research response v1 to the approved requester
inputs: approved research response v1 and recipient

tasks.design: Configure native cross-index search and catalogue citation export in the library discovery system in {OTHER}. The librarian still clarifies the request, reads unusual sources and verifies meaning; checked citation metadata fills the {EMAIL} response around the librarian's actual findings before the separate send.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeat queries and citation copying span several indexes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing discovery filters and citation export can reuse actual record metadata.
tasks.still_hard: Rare sources, ambiguous identities and unavailable material require investigation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a plausible-looking source does not answer the question.
tasks.altitude: Less query repetition and reference formatting; the librarian still owns source verification.

reach.learn: Provenance and limits of archival finding aids

evidence.claim: Native library discovery filters and citation export can reduce repeated searches and reference formatting.

assumptions: Boundary includes clarifying the question, searching, verifying sources and replying. Shares are provisional, not a measured reference-service baseline.

Catalogue owners and licensed publishers already produce record IDs, titles, authors, dates, holdings/access and stable source locators. The librarian supplies search terms in s1-s2 and verifies actual works in s3; unresolved records are checked manually, not generated.
s4 copies only checked citation metadata and response headers. The librarian authors the actual finding and limitation; a native template suffices, with no model answer inferred from abstracts.
{OTHER} means library catalogue/discovery and licensed indexes. s4 approves the completed message and recipient; edits void approval. Existing search runtime and the actual send earn no saving.
unknowns: Native cross-index coverage and availability of rare sources
research_questions: Which query and citation operations are repeated across the existing indexes?

already_counted.description: Review search results and adjust actual queries
Verify source meaning and pursue missing evidence
Author and check actual research response

incremental.description: Maintain index connections and citation-field mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central repeated-search reduction 14 plus citation/header reuse 4.2 less 1 upkeep = 17.2. Low assumes rare material is mostly outside connected indexes and citations need manual correction; substantive verification stays whole.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop and troubleshoot library information-access aids.

steps.what: Define or diagnose the actual information-access problem and specify selected resources, annotations, tutorial actions and intended user journeys
inputs: user access need or reproduced fault

steps.what: Build or maintain the specified database view, bibliography, web pathfinder or tutorial using selected records and explicit navigation and content
Troubleshoot the completed access aid with representative searches, links, user permissions and tutorial tasks; correct and retest failures
Approve the exact tested access aid v1, resource descriptions, accessible user journey and intended repository and public release destinations
Save the exact approved access-aid package v1 to the internal development repository
Release the exact approved access aid v1 at the approved public library access destination

tasks.design: Test native catalogue views, bibliography exports and {CMS} page/tutorial templates before writing software. They render the librarian's selected records, actual annotations and explicit tutorial steps; the librarian reproduces faults and tests the complete aid before distinct save and public-release actions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Similar paths and resource lists are rebuilt by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views and reusable page structures can render explicit content.
tasks.still_hard: Resource selection, access failures and whether the aid teaches the intended task need user-context testing.
tasks.human_edge: Diagnose why a real user cannot find or use the information.

ambition.what: No additional publishing or system-administration rights.

tasks.altitude: Less repetitive assembly; resource judgement and troubleshooting stay with the librarian.

reach.task: Maintain access records and assist users
reach.learn: How to reproduce access failures and document a tested fix

evidence.claim: Native catalogue views and page templates can assemble explicitly selected library resources and navigation.

assumptions: Boundary covers development, maintenance and troubleshooting of an access aid through approved release. Shares are provisional. Custom software beyond native template support remains manual within s2; its authoring is not assumed eliminated.

The librarian produces selected record IDs, actual annotations, navigation and tutorial action sequence in s1. Catalogue owners supply title, author, locator and access terms; missing data or unrecorded tutorial steps are checked and written manually in s1-s2.

{OTHER} means library catalogue, tutorial tools and the internal access-aid development repository. The 40% s2 cut assumes repeat views or pages can use native structure; it does not shorten content decisions or test work.

s4 follows completion and retesting and binds exact content and destinations. Edits void approval. Ordinary save, actual release and existing runtime earn no saving; permission changes require separate authorised actions.
unknowns: Which aids fit native templates rather than custom software
Actual access permissions and accessibility requirements
research_questions: Can the current platform render the required pathfinder and tutorial without custom code?

already_counted.description: Correct candidate assembly and unsupported native cases
Troubleshoot and retest actual access behaviour

incremental.description: Maintain reusable layouts and metadata mappings beyond ordinary aid upkeep

approvals.approved_version: access-aid release package v1: repository package
access-aid release package v1: public content and destination

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central 35 assembly hours at 40% reduction less 1.5 upkeep = 12.5. Low assumes bespoke databases and software dominate and native templates cover little; requirements, fault diagnosis, testing and release keep full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Investigate actual library service problems, current procedures, user needs and applicable organisational requirements
Decide the proposed library policy choices, responsibilities, exceptions and explicit procedure actions
Write a coherent library policy and procedure draft expressing the actual decisions, responsibilities, actions and exceptions

loop.purpose: Express supplied library policy decisions as readable procedures
loop.input: actual decisions, roles, explicit action sequences, exceptions and checked source requirements
loop.output: candidate policy draft with traceable requirements
loop.check: Librarian checks that duties, discretion, exceptions and action order preserve the actual decisions and do not create unsupported obligations or rights
loop.stop: One draft and one correction; unresolved meaning is written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Variable policy rationale and exception wording require coherent prose; a template only supplies headings. Policy choices and procedure actions are supplied by the librarian.

steps.what: Review the exact completed policy draft v1 for requirement fidelity, workable procedures, responsibilities and intended internal draft destination
Save the exact checked library policy draft v1 to the internal policy-development folder

tasks.design: Use the existing policy template in {DOCS}, with a bounded loop only for coherent wording of the librarian's actual policy and procedure decisions. The librarian checks substantive meaning after the complete draft exists, then saves that version; institutional adoption and publication remain separate authority decisions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Policy prose is repeatedly written around decisions and existing requirements.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting loop can produce traceable prose from explicit choices.
tasks.still_hard: Resolving service trade-offs and making workable exceptions remain human work.
tasks.human_edge: Choose fair, useful library procedures and recognise unintended restrictions.
tasks.altitude: Less prose composition; needs assessment and policy choices stay with the librarian.

reach.learn: How provenance and access constraints affect procedure design

evidence.claim: A bounded model can draft coherent policy prose from explicit professional decisions with substantive human checking.

assumptions: Boundary is policy development through a saved checked draft, not adoption or public release. Actual stakeholder investigation and policy choices are included, not free inputs. Shares are provisional.

The librarian produces actual problem, affected users, responsibilities, decisions, exception limits and procedure actions in s1-s2. Organisational owners provide current approved requirements in {DOCS}; missing or disputed rules are resolved manually.
Native headings and document structure are tested first. The model only writes prose, not new obligations or legal conclusions. s3 includes capture/correction and s4 final semantic review.
Any edit voids the save approval. Same-system save and runtime earn no saving; any later adoption, send or publication requires its own completed-version gate and separate action.
unknowns: Institutional adoption process and frequency of repeated policy drafting
research_questions: Can the draft preserve actual exception discretion without adding obligations?

already_counted.description: Correct policy draft against actual decisions
Check completed policy meaning and procedure workability

incremental.description: Maintain policy-drafting constraints and sample semantic checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central 30 drafting hours at 45% reduction less 1 upkeep = 12.5. Low assumes contested exceptions require mostly manual rewriting; actual investigation, policy choices and final review remain whole.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Find current library continuing-education classes, workshops or professional meetings relevant to the librarian's learning needs
Choose the appropriate actual event and check its completed registration details, schedule, fee authorisation and organiser recipient
inputs: registration details and authorised fee limit

steps.what: Submit the exact approved registration package v1 to the approved event organiser
Attend the class or professional meeting, practise new skills, participate in discussions and reflect on their application to library work
Write and check actual learning notes, participation dates and any evidenced completion after the event
Save the exact checked actual development record v1 in the internal learning record

tasks.design: Configure native topic and date filters for existing course listings in {LMS} and organiser course portals in {OTHER}. The librarian chooses and authorises the completed registration, participates personally and records actual learning afterwards; booking, participation and completion remain distinct phases.
tasks.previous_blocker: Relevant event listings can require repeated browsing.
tasks.enabler_now: Native topic/date filters can narrow actual course listings.
tasks.still_hard: Learning, professional relationships and judging relevance require participation.
tasks.human_edge: Connect new ideas to real library problems and colleagues.

ambition.what: No additional qualification or spending authority.

tasks.altitude: Professional participation still takes essentially the same time.

reach.learn: Evaluate new methods and their evidence before applying them

evidence.claim: Native course topic and date filters can shorten repeated listing navigation without replacing learning.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual course selection, registration, participation and learning record. Shares are provisional; no planned course is labelled attended.

Organisers supply actual title, date, format, topic, fee and registration recipient through existing listings; missing details are checked manually in s1-s2. The librarian supplies learning needs and actual registration fields.

s2 checks the completed booking details and existing authorised fee limit; if manager approval is required its own work must be retained, not inferred. No payment automation or new external charge is assumed.

The librarian produces actual notes and participation/completion evidence in s4-s5. Registration never supplies completion. Edits void either approval. Ordinary saves, submission and runtime earn no saving.
unknowns: Which courses and association events are discoverable through native filters
research_questions: Is event browsing repetitive enough to justify maintaining saved filters?

already_counted.description: Choose and approve completed registration details
Write and check actual learning record

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central 8 listing-search hours at 25% reduction less 0.3 upkeep = 1.7. Low assumes the librarian already knows the event or listings need manual checking; participation and learning notes keep full effort.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The librarian spends less time repeating searches and assembling access aids or drafts while retaining source verification, policy choices and professional learning.
reach: Archivists: connect source provenance with reliable reference answers
Library Technicians: share reproducible access tests
skills_to_grow: Substantive review of generated policy prose
role.ambitious_version: A librarian who makes reliable information easier to reach and explains what the available evidence can actually support.
